purpose: Preliminary geographic search screens, not a model, drilling prediction, valuation or parcel recommendation.
bounds_format: [south, west, north, east] degrees; rectangular analyst-selected windows, not parcel boundaries or aquifer boundaries.
caveats: Counts are source records, not unique wells; areas can overlap.
No drilling success rate is calculated: failure reporting is incomplete.
All yields are historical reported observations; water quality and sustainable withdrawal are unproven.
Road proximity does not establish legal access or road condition.
Area boundaries are transparent search windows, not a probability heat map.

areas.name: Highway 118 / Terlingua Ranch Road junction
areas.road: Intersection of Highway 118 and the paved western end of Terlingua Ranch Road.
areas.thesis: Cheap-land and road-access comparison only; the retrieved water evidence is too weak for a water-led recommendation.
areas.caution: Only three water-well source records within three straight-line miles of this junction: an 880-foot dry record in 2005, a 4 gpm bailed report from 1976 with questionable location, and a 1 gpm jetted report at 420 feet in 2022.

areas.name: Terlingua Ghost Town / Long Draw / FM 170
areas.road: FM 170 plus Long Draw and South County Road; proximity to the highway does not verify a parcel entrance or easement.
areas.thesis: A deep historical public-supply well demonstrates large reported flow in the district; contiguous land near town could support a land-assembly or existing-supply strategy.
areas.caution: The 375 gpm example is a 1999 test at 1,160 feet, not a forecast on adjoining land. The SDR and GWDB examples document the same well. A large existing utility well is not available supply for a buyer.

areas.name: North Corazones / roads north and east of Terlingua Ranch Lodge
areas.road: Terlingua Ranch Road approach, then local ranch roads. Lodge says first 13 of its 16-mile approach from Highway 118 are paved; its final 3 miles are unpaved.
areas.thesis: Potential larger-acreage search where some 2020-2021 reports show 65-100 gpm; prioritize parcels with an existing independently tested well and straightforward access.
areas.caution: A mixed patchwork: dry holes at 500 and 682 feet and a plugged dry hole at 1,005 feet appear in the same screen. Lodge public-supply records do not establish water entitlements for new parcels.

areas.name: Lajitas / Comanche Mesa / FM 170
areas.road: FM 170 and Comanche Mesa local roads; private access and ownership require confirmation.
areas.thesis: Strong historical deep-well pump-test evidence; a comparison district for an existing-water or partnership strategy.
areas.caution: 400-450 gpm tests are from 2001 at roughly 984-1,040 feet, with cross-database duplicate records. Neither cheap land nor access to these supplies is established; do not prioritize solely because yields are largest.
